summary: Russia launched a massive multi-axis air attack across Ukraine involving Shahed drones, cruise missiles, and jet UAVs targeting at least ten oblasts. A Russian strike on a minibus in Kherson killed four civilians and wounded four. Ukraine secured the return of 103 prisoners of war from Russian captivity in a coordinated exchange.
key_points: Massive Russian air attack with Shaheds, cruise missiles, and jet UAVs reported across Kyiv, Kharkiv, Poltava, Cherkasy, Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Chernihiv, Zhytomyr, and Rivne oblasts. (Source: @eRadarrua/106222)
Russian strike on a minibus in Kherson killed four people and wounded four others. (Source: @UkraineNow/83523)
103 Ukrainian defenders, including Azovstal and multi-front veterans, returned from Russian captivity in a prisoner exchange. (Source: @UkraineNow/83528)
Verkhovna Rada appointed Yevhen Khmara as Defense Minister and Andriy Sybiha as Foreign Minister amid protests. (Source: @UkraineNow/83538)
Russian MoD claimed liberation of Novonikolaevka in Donetsk Oblast; DeepState map confirms enemy advances near Kalenyky and Tsvetkovo. (Source: @tass_agency/391159)
Moscow Mayor Sobyanin reported 250 Ukrainian drones targeted Moscow region overnight, most destroyed at far approaches. (Source: @tass_agency/391173)
Former Defense Minister Fedorov declared opposition to Zelensky, demanding elections; corruption allegations surfaced against Presidential Office deputy Mudraya. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32581)
Government plans TCC reform to reduce forced mobilization, digitalize operations, and emphasize recruitment per MP Shulyak. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32564)

sections.executive_summary: Russia launched a massive multi-axis air attack across Ukraine involving Shahed drones, cruise missiles, and jet UAVs targeting at least ten oblasts. A Russian strike on a minibus in Kherson killed four civilians and wounded four. Ukraine secured the return of 103 prisoners of war from Russian captivity in a coordinated exchange.

points: Ukraine welcomed back 103 prisoners of war from Russian captivity, including defenders of Mariupol, Donetsk, Luhansk, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Dnipro, and Sumy directions, per the Coordination Headquarters. (Source: @UkraineNow/83528)

The Verkhovna Rada confirmed Yevhen Khmara as Minister of Defense and Andriy Sybiha as Minister of Foreign Affairs, prompting protests outside parliament with chants of "Shame!". (Source: @UkraineNow/83538, @ukr_leaks_eng/32577)

Former Defense Minister Mikhail Fedorov publicly opposed President Zelensky, declaring a "crisis of governance" and demanding immediate elections, with a rally held near the Verkhovna Rada in his support. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32581, @ukr_leaks_eng/32567)

Deputy Head of the Presidential Office Iryna Mudraya allegedly attempted to post bail for detained former Energy Minister Herman Halushchenko via shell companies, per a new Ukr Leaks investigation. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32576)

A mobilized child anesthesiologist, Dmytro Sysoniuk, died after falling from the fifth floor of a training center in Vinnytsia Oblast following his hospital's loss of critical status and a VLK ruling him fit for rear service. (Source: @UkraineNow/83541)

Servant of the People MP Elena Shulyak stated the government plans to reform Territorial Recruitment Centers by reducing "busification," digitalizing operations, and shifting focus from forced mobilization to recruitment. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32564)
Russia informed Ukraine of the whereabouts of 79 Ukrainian servicemen previously considered missing without trace, per Commissioner Lubinets. (Source: @UkraineNow/83552)

Russian forces conducted a large-scale combined air attack launching Shahed-type UAVs, jet UAVs, and cruise missiles from multiple directions including Bryansk, Belgorod, and occupied territories, targeting central, northern, and eastern Ukrainian oblasts. (Source: @eRadarrua/106264, @kpszsu/73541)
The Russian Ministry of Defense claimed its forces liberated the settlement of Novonikolaevka in the Donetsk People's Republic. (Source: @tass_agency/391159)

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported that 250 Ukrainian UAVs targeted the Moscow region between 20:30 and 07:30 MSK, with the majority destroyed on distant approaches by air defenses. (Source: @tass_agency/391173)
Russian forces struck a minibus in Kherson city, killing four civilians and wounding four others, according to Ukrainian officials. (Source: @UkraineNow/83523)
A Tornado-S multiple launch rocket system strike was reported on Nikopol in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/70659)
Russian missiles were tracked crossing the Chernihiv and Zhytomyr oblasts toward Kyiv region, with multiple groups of cruise missiles and jet UAVs detected. (Source: @eRadarrua/106223, @kpszsu/73541)
The Kremlin stated there was no announcement yet regarding a possible visit by US envoys Witkoff and Kushner, noting such meetings require preparation. (Source: @tass_agency/391135)
DeepState map update indicates Russian forces advanced near the settlements of Kalenyky and Tsvetkovo in Donetsk Oblast. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23757)
Russian MoD announced the liberation of Novonikolaevka in the Donetsk People's Republic, suggesting further consolidation in the area. (Source: @tass_agency/391159)
Russian missile strikes targeted the Kharkiv Oblast vicinity of Balakliya and Berestyn, flying westward toward Poltava Oblast. (Source: @kpszsu/73516, @kpszsu/73518)
Multiple cruise missile groups were detected in Poltava Oblast near Novy Sanzhary and Orzhytsia, on courses toward Kyiv region. (Source: @eRadarrua/106222, @kpszsu/73534)
Jet UAVs were reported over Poltava Oblast near Semenivka moving toward Chernihiv Oblast, and south of Kremenchuk on a southern course. (Source: @kpszsu/73534, @kpszsu/73517)
Missiles on the border of Cherkasy and Kirovohrad oblasts flew westward; others near Bozhedarivka in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast turned toward Kirovohrad Oblast. (Source: @kpszsu/73509)
Missiles in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast changed course toward Kryvyi Rih, indicating potential targeting of critical infrastructure. (Source: @kpszsu/73511)
Two jet UAVs from Bryansk Oblast flew past Slavutych toward Kyiv/Brovary, per eRadar monitoring. (Source: @eRadarrua/106264)
Three Shahed UAVs from Chernihiv Oblast crossed into Kyiv Oblast on a course for Kyiv/Brovary. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/70662)
Jet UAVs detected in northern Zhytomyr Oblast moving westward; western Chernihiv Oblast UAVs heading toward Kyiv Oblast. (Source: @kpszsu/73541)
A reactive Shahed from Zhytomyr Oblast moved toward northern Rivne Oblast. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/70660)

Kyiv Oblast air defense engaged multiple groups: reactive UAVs (3 groups per eRadar), a Shahed from Brovary to Troieshchyna, and a new Shahed from the north to Desnyansky district. (Source: @eRadarrua/106223, @mon1tor_ua/70657, @mon1tor_ua/70647)
Missiles near Baryshivka in Kyiv Oblast flew westward toward Kyiv. (Source: @kpszsu/73527)
Combat air defense operations ongoing past Slavutych and Desna toward Brovary district with at least five jet UAVs. (Source: @eRadarrua/106282)
Russian strike on a minibus in Kherson city resulted in four deaths and four injuries. (Source: @UkraineNow/83523)
Tornado-S MLRS strike reported on Nikopol in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/70659)
Missiles tracked near Bozhedarivka in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast heading toward Kirovohrad Oblast. (Source: @kpszsu/73509)
Missiles in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast diverted course toward Kryvyi Rih. (Source: @kpszsu/73511)
Jet UAVs detected in Kirovohrad Oblast near Dolynska; in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast near Reshetylivka and north of Kryvyi Rih. (Source: @eRadarrua/106276, @kpszsu/73517)
Three jet UAVs from Cherkasy Oblast moved toward southern Kyiv Oblast. (Source: @eRadarrua/106280)
A Shahed UAV from Donbas entered Brovary area in Kyiv Oblast. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/70655)

Massive overnight air attack: multiple waves of Shahed-136/131 type UAVs (reactive), jet-powered UAVs, and Kh-101/555 cruise missiles launched from Russian territory and occupied areas. (Source: @eRadarrua/106222, @kpszsu/73541)
At least four groups of two cruise missiles each tracked in Poltava Oblast past Novy Sanzhary toward Kyiv region. (Source: @eRadarrua/106222)

Kyiv Oblast faced three groups of reactive UAVs; Chernihiv Oblast three groups; Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Kharkiv oblasts each two groups of reactive UAVs. (Source: @eRadarrua/106223, @eRadarrua/106226)

Jet UAVs reported in Obukhiv and Boryspil districts of Kyiv Oblast on northwest course; in Brovary district; near Slavutych and Desna toward Brovary (minimum 5). (Source: @kpszsu/73541, @kpszsu/73517, @eRadarrua/106282)
Cruise missile detected near Drabiv in Cherkasy Oblast on course to Boryspil; last group of cruise missiles in Poltava Oblast also toward Kyiv region. (Source: @eRadarrua/106251, @eRadarrua/106246)
Missiles near Balakliya and Berestyn in Kharkiv Oblast flew westward toward Poltava Oblast. (Source: @kpszsu/73516, @kpszsu/73518)
Moscow region air defenses engaged 250 Ukrainian UAVs overnight, majority destroyed at far approaches per Mayor Sobyanin. (Source: @tass_agency/391173)

key_developments: Russia executed a massive coordinated air assault across at least ten Ukrainian oblasts using Shahed drones, jet UAVs, and cruise missiles, with active air defense combat reported over Kyiv, Chernihiv, Poltava, and Dnipropetrovsk regions. (Source: @eRadarrua/106222, @eRadarrua/106223)
Russian strike on a civilian minibus in Kherson killed four and wounded four, underscoring continued targeting of urban infrastructure in southern Ukraine. (Source: @UkraineNow/83523)
Ukraine recovered 103 prisoners of war from Russian captivity, including defenders from Mariupol and multiple front lines, in a negotiated exchange. (Source: @UkraineNow/83528)

Verkhovna Rada approved Yevhen Khmara as Defense Minister and Andriy Sybiha as Foreign Minister despite public protests and opposition from former Defense Minister Fedorov. (Source: @UkraineNow/83538, @ukr_leaks_eng/32577)
Russian forces claimed capture of Novonikolaevka in Donetsk Oblast; DeepState mapping confirms tactical advances near Kalenyky and Tsvetkovo. (Source: @tass_agency/391159, @DeepStateUA/23757)
Moscow air defenses intercepted 250 Ukrainian drones overnight, the largest reported single-night UAV attack on the Russian capital region. (Source: @tass_agency/391173)

Corruption allegations against Presidential Office deputy Iryna Mudraya and former Defense Minister Fedorov's public break with Zelensky signal deepening domestic political instability. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32576, @ukr_leaks_eng/32581)
sections.threat_assessment: The scale and complexity of Russia's latest air attack — combining Shaheds, jet UAVs, and cruise missiles across a broad front — indicates an intent to saturate Ukrainian air defenses and strike critical infrastructure deep in the rear. Simultaneous ground advances in eastern Donetsk Oblast suggest Russia is maintaining offensive pressure while Ukraine manages a high-tempo air defense battle. The domestic political turbulence in Kyiv, including the controversial defense minister appointment and corruption scandals, risks undermining command cohesion and Western confidence at a critical juncture.
sections.regional_response: Moscow's claim of destroying 250 Ukrainian drones over its territory signals a significant escalation in Ukrainian long-range strike capabilities, likely prompting enhanced Russian air defense posture around strategic hubs. The prisoner exchange demonstrates that backchannel negotiations remain functional despite battlefield intensity. Western allies will closely monitor Ukraine's political stability following the defense ministry shakeup and corruption allegations, as these affect aid delivery timelines and military reform credibility.
sections.intelligence_notes: The use of jet-powered UAVs (likely Russian "Geran-2" variants with turbojet engines) alongside traditional Shaheds and cruise missiles reflects an evolving Russian strike package designed to complicate interception. The density of threats over Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Poltava oblasts suggests prioritization of central Ukraine's energy and command infrastructure. The DeepState-confirmed advances near Kalenyky and Tsvetkovo, combined with the Novonikolaevka claim, indicate a persistent Russian push toward the administrative borders of Donetsk Oblast. The TCC reform discussion hints at Ukrainian manpower challenges affecting mobilization sustainability.
